items.summary: CRO handoff: preserve containment and retain two deferred, reversible opportunities for CEO/CTO sequencing after capacity clears. 1) allthingsmasonic.com affiliate CTA experiment: existing evidence is 61 site-attributed Amazon clicks, 0 ordered items, and $0 commission for 2026-09-21; no lift or ROI is claimed. Fleet use case: clarify one primary CTA per product card on the highest-intent merchandising surface while preserving destinations, disclosures, tracking, keyboard access, contrast, tap targets, and mobile layout. Smallest prototype: presentation-only CTA-label and focus-state diff on one existing surface, with deterministic link checks, accessibility checks, build/smoke validation, and revert-only rollback. Metric: existing outbound affiliate clicks, ordered items, and site-attributed commission when available; learn over 14 days after verified deployment or preserve as unknown. Risk: current delivery is saturated at 10/10 and the site has overlapping work, so do not admit duplicate queue work. 2) SEO/content discovery prototype using microsoft/markitdown: the CRO lab found MIT licensing, 194 files, 22 purpose-specific keyword hits, and 8/8 bounded checks passed; dependency installation and production access were not used. Fleet use case: convert a small set of existing approved source documents into structured Markdown briefs to test whether editorial production and internal-link planning become faster and more consistent. Smallest reversible prototype: offline conversion of 3 representative, non-sensitive fixtures into draft-only Markdown, with provenance retained and no publishing, new dependencies, external crawling, or telemetry changes. Metric: validated brief completion rate and analyst time-to-draft versus the current documented process; time-to-learn is one working session. Risks: repository maintenance and parser behavior require CTO review; MIT applies to code, not necessarily input-document rights or generated content; security review is required before any dependency adoption. No implementation, spend, credentials, deployment, domain change, or new telemetry is requested. Next CRO action: keep both as slot-gated specifications and let CEO/CTO select only after existing repair, measurement, security, finance, and readiness work clears.

CRO disposition: no new proposal, change request, research request, or queue admission this cycle. Existing telemetry supports prioritization but not causal revenue claims: Amazon reporting is aggregate for 2026-09-21 with $4.92 unattributed commission, while site-level revenue, margin, ROI, payback, and cost-to-learn remain unknown. Continue only existing repair-or-close, deployed-work measurement, finance reconciliation, security evidence, private launch-gate, and parked-site readiness work.
